name: Jesus Christ
role: Son of God and Son of Mary · Nazareth
title: The Teacher
summary: The Word made flesh, true God and true man. He taught in parables and by his life, died on the Cross for our sins, and rose from the dead. Every other teacher on this page points to him.

name: Abraham
title: Our Father in Faith
summary: Called by God to leave his homeland, he trusted the promise that his descendants would be as many as the stars. Ready even to offer his son Isaac, he is the father of all who believe.

name: Moses
title: Lawgiver
summary: Raised in Pharaoh's court, he met God in the burning bush and led Israel out of slavery in Egypt. On Mount Sinai he received the Law and the Ten Commandments. He appeared with Elijah at the Transfiguration.

name: David
title: The Psalmist
summary: A shepherd boy who killed Goliath and became Israel's greatest king. Many Psalms bear his name, and God promised that his throne would last forever, a promise fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David.

name: Elijah
summary: Defended the worship of the one God against the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, and was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. The Carmelites look to him as their spiritual father.

name: Isaiah
summary: Foretold a virgin who would bear a son called Emmanuel, and the Suffering Servant "wounded for our iniquities." The Church reads him throughout Advent.

name: Jeremiah
title: The Weeping Prophet
summary: Called as a young man to warn Judah before Jerusalem fell in 587 BC, he suffered rejection and prison for it. He foretold a new covenant, written not on stone but on the heart.

name: Joachim
summary: By tradition, the father of the Blessed Virgin Mary. His name comes not from Scripture but from the second-century Protoevangelium of James. Honored with St. Anne on July 26.

name: Anne
summary: By tradition, the mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary, known from the second-century Protoevangelium of James. Grandmother of Jesus, and patron of mothers and grandparents.

name: Zechariah
summary: A priest of the Temple who doubted the angel's promise of a son and was struck mute until John was born. His canticle, the Benedictus, is prayed every morning in the Liturgy of the Hours.

name: Elizabeth
summary: Mother of John the Baptist in her old age. Filled with the Holy Spirit when Mary visited, she cried out "Blessed art thou among women," words now part of the Hail Mary.

name: Joseph
title: Guardian of the Redeemer
summary: A just man and a carpenter who took Mary as his wife and raised Jesus as his own. He obeyed God's word given in dreams, and Scripture records no word he spoke. Patron of the universal Church.

name: John the Baptist
title: Forerunner of the Lord
summary: Preached repentance in the wilderness and baptized Jesus in the Jordan, pointing to him as "the Lamb of God." Beheaded by Herod Antipas for condemning his unlawful marriage.

name: The Blessed Virgin Mary
title: Seat of Wisdom
summary: Said yes to God at the Annunciation and became the Mother of Jesus. She kept all these things in her heart, stood by the Cross, and prayed with the Apostles at Pentecost. The first and model disciple.

name: Mary Magdalene
title: Apostle to the Apostles
summary: Freed by Jesus from seven demons, she followed him to the Cross and was the first to see him risen. Sent to tell the disciples, she is honored as the Apostle to the Apostles. Pope Francis raised her day to a feast in 2016.

name: Peter
title: Prince of the Apostles
summary: A Galilean fisherman whom Jesus named the rock on which he would build his Church. He denied Christ three times, was forgiven, and led the Apostles after Pentecost. The first Pope, crucified in Rome under Nero.

name: Andrew
title: The First-Called
summary: A fisherman and disciple of John the Baptist who brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus. By tradition crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras in Greece. Patron of Scotland.

name: James the Greater
title: Son of Thunder
summary: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, with Peter one of the three closest to Jesus at the Transfiguration and in Gethsemane. The first Apostle martyred, by order of Herod Agrippa. His shrine at Santiago de Compostela draws pilgrims from around the world.

name: John
title: The Beloved Disciple
summary: Son of Zebedee, the disciple whom Jesus loved, who stood at the Cross and took Mary into his home. Tradition credits him with the Gospel of John, three letters, and Revelation. By tradition, the only Apostle not martyred.

name: Philip
summary: From Bethsaida, he brought Nathanael to Jesus and at the Last Supper asked, "Lord, show us the Father." By tradition martyred at Hierapolis in Asia Minor.

name: Bartholomew
summary: Often identified with Nathanael, whom Jesus called "an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no guile." Tradition says he preached as far as India and Armenia, where he was martyred.

name: Matthew
summary: A tax collector at Capernaum who left his booth when Jesus said "Follow me." The Gospel of Matthew, written for Jewish Christians, bears his name. Traditions differ on where he preached and died.

name: Thomas
summary: Doubted the Resurrection until he saw the risen Christ, then confessed "My Lord and my God." Tradition holds that he carried the Gospel to India, where he was martyred near Chennai.

name: James the Less
summary: Son of Alphaeus. Catholic tradition identifies him with James "the brother of the Lord," who led the church in Jerusalem and is credited with the Letter of James. Martyred in Jerusalem.

name: Jude Thaddeus
summary: Also called Thaddeus, he asked Jesus at the Last Supper why he would show himself to the disciples and not to the world. Tradition links him to the Letter of Jude. Invoked as patron of hopeless causes.

name: Simon the Zealot
summary: Called "the Zealot" in the Gospels. Western tradition says he preached in Persia with St. Jude, and the two share a feast on October 28.

name: Matthias
summary: Chosen by lot to take the place of Judas among the Twelve. He had followed Jesus from his baptism by John to the Ascension. Little else is known of him for certain.

name: Stephen
title: The First Martyr
summary: One of the seven chosen to serve the poor of the Jerusalem church. Stoned to death for his witness, he forgave his killers as he died, while Saul of Tarsus looked on.

name: Paul
title: Apostle to the Gentiles
summary: A Pharisee who persecuted the Church until the risen Christ met him on the road to Damascus. His missionary journeys carried the Gospel across the Roman world, and his letters make up nearly half the books of the New Testament. Beheaded in Rome.

name: Barnabas
title: Son of Encouragement
summary: A Levite from Cyprus who sold his field for the Church and vouched for Paul when others feared him. He went with Paul on the first missionary journey. By tradition martyred in Cyprus.

name: Mark
summary: John Mark, a companion of Paul and Barnabas and later of Peter, whose preaching his Gospel is said to record. By tradition he founded the church of Alexandria and was martyred there.

name: Luke
title: The Beloved Physician
summary: A physician and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. His Gospel gives the fullest account of Jesus' birth and of Mary.

name: Timothy
summary: Son of a Jewish mother and a Greek father, he became Paul's closest companion and co-worker. Paul wrote two letters to him, and tradition makes him the first bishop of Ephesus, martyred there.

name: Irenaeus of Lyon
title: Doctor of Unity
summary: Against Heresies refuted Gnosticism and named apostolic succession and the rule of faith as the test of true teaching.

Includes the line: "The Son is truly God, from the true God, Light from Light."

name: Athanasius
title: Father of Orthodoxy
summary: Held to Nicaea's teaching that the Son is one in being with the Father, through five exiles. Wrote On the Incarnation.

Includes the line: "The Son of God became man so that we might become God."

name: Ephrem the Syrian
title: Harp of the Holy Spirit
summary: Taught doctrine through hymns and poetry, with a deep devotion to Mary.

name: Basil the Great
summary: Wrote the Rule that shaped Eastern monastic life, and On the Holy Spirit. Founded hospitals for the poor.

Includes the line: "A tree is known by its fruit; a Christian is known by his deeds."

summary: His Catechetical Lectures remain a model for forming new Christians, rich on Baptism and the Eucharist.

title: The Theologian
summary: Five Theological Orations gave the Church its language for the Trinity, affirmed at Constantinople in 381.

name: Ambrose of Milan
summary: A preacher and hymn writer who baptized Augustine and defended the Church's freedom from imperial control.

name: John Chrysostom
title: Golden Mouth
summary: The East's greatest preacher. Homilies on Scripture and on care for the poor. A Divine Liturgy bears his name.

Includes the line: "If you cannot find Christ in the beggar at the church door, you will not find Him in the chalice."

name: Jerome
summary: Translated the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate). "Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ."

name: Augustine of Hippo
title: Doctor of Grace
summary: Confessions and City of God. Taught on grace, original sin, and the heart that is restless until it rests in God.

name: Cyril of Alexandria
title: Doctor of the Incarnation
summary: Led the Council of Ephesus (431), which proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God.

name: Peter Chrysologus
title: Golden-Worded
summary: Short, vivid sermons on the Gospels, the Creed and the Incarnation.

name: Leo the Great
summary: His Tome at Chalcedon (451) defined Christ as one person in two natures, divine and human.

name: Gregory the Great
summary: Pastoral Rule on caring for souls. Sent missionaries to England and called the pope "servant of the servants of God."

name: Isidore of Seville
summary: His Etymologies, an encyclopedia of all knowledge, carried classical learning into the Middle Ages.

name: Bede the Venerable
title: Father of English History
summary: Ecclesiastical History of the English People and Scripture commentaries. Popularized dating years A.D.

name: John Damascene
title: Doctor of the Assumption
summary: Defended sacred images against iconoclasm and summed up Eastern theology in The Fount of Knowledge.

name: Gregory of Narek
summary: His Book of Lamentations is a searching prayer of repentance and trust in mercy.

name: Peter Damian
summary: Called clergy and Church leaders to reform and taught a demanding monastic spirituality.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
title: Father of Scholasticism
summary: "Faith seeking understanding." His Why God Became Man explains the Atonement.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
title: Mellifluous Doctor
summary: Led Cistercian reform. His Sermons on the Song of Songs teach the love of God, and he had a deep Marian devotion.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
title: Sibyl of the Rhine
summary: Visionary theology (Scivias), sacred music, and writings on medicine and nature.

name: Anthony of Padua
title: Evangelical Doctor
summary: A Franciscan preacher whose sermons, saturated with Scripture, won back many from heresy.

resources.title: St. Anthony of Padua
resources.note: His life, with notes on his writings.

name: Bonaventure
title: Seraphic Doctor
summary: The Journey of the Mind into God. Joined Franciscan love with rigorous theology.

name: Thomas Aquinas
title: Angelic Doctor
summary: The Summa Theologiae. Showed faith and reason in harmony and wrote Eucharistic hymns still sung today.

name: Albert the Great
title: Universal Doctor
summary: Joined natural science and theology, taught Aquinas, and is patron of scientists.

name: Catherine of Siena
summary: The Dialogue. A laywoman who urged the pope to return to Rome from Avignon.

name: John of Ávila
title: Apostle of Andalusia
summary: Renewed the training of priests and guided many saints. Wrote Audi, Filia.

name: Teresa of Ávila
title: Doctor of Prayer
summary: The Interior Castle. Reformed the Carmelites and taught prayer as friendship with God.

name: John of the Cross
title: Mystical Doctor
summary: Dark Night of the Soul. How God purifies and draws the soul into union through darkness and dryness.

name: Peter Canisius
title: Second Apostle of Germany
summary: Wrote catechisms for ordinary believers that renewed Catholic life after the Reformation.

name: Lawrence of Brindisi
title: Apostolic Doctor
summary: A preacher fluent in many languages. Wrote on Mary and Scripture and served as a peacemaker.

name: Robert Bellarmine
summary: His Controversies gave clear, charitable answers to Protestant objections. Also wrote catechisms.

name: Francis de Sales
title: Patron of writers
summary: Introduction to the Devout Life: holiness for people in every walk of life, including at work and at home.

name: Alphonsus Liguori
title: Most Zealous Doctor
summary: Moral theology marked by mercy. Founded the Redemptorists and wrote The Glories of Mary. Patron of confessors.

name: John Henry Newman
summary: A convert who wrote on the development of doctrine, conscience, and how we come to believe (Grammar of Assent).

name: Thérèse of Lisieux
title: The Little Flower
summary: Story of a Soul. The Little Way: holiness through small acts of love and complete trust.

name: Justin Martyr
title: Apologist
summary: A philosopher who became a Christian and defended the faith to the emperors. His First Apology gives the earliest description of the Mass.

name: Origen
summary: The early Church's most prolific biblical scholar. His Hexapla and commentaries shaped how the Church reads Scripture, though some of his speculations were later condemned.

name: Gregory of Nyssa
title: Father of Fathers
summary: Brother of Basil the Great and one of the Cappadocian Fathers. He defended the Trinity at the Council of Constantinople in 381 and wrote of the soul's endless ascent into God in The Life of Moses.

printable.alt: One-page printable on St. Gregory of Nyssa (c. 335–c. 395), Bishop of Nyssa and one of the Cappadocian Fathers, covering who he was, his major works, why he is important, key themes, and his legacy. Includes the line: "The true vision of the One we seek consists in this: in not seeing, because the One desired transcends all knowledge."

resources.note: A summary of Christian doctrine for teachers of the faith.

resources.note: On the human person as made in God's image.

resources.title: St. Gregory of Nyssa
resources.note: His life and writings.

name: Maximus the Confessor
summary: Defended Christ's full human will against Monothelitism and was mutilated and exiled for it. The Third Council of Constantinople (681) upheld his teaching.

name: Edith Stein
title: Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
summary: A Jewish philosopher and student of Husserl who became Catholic and a Carmelite. She wrote Finite and Eternal Being and died at Auschwitz. Co-patroness of Europe.

name: Joseph Ratzinger
title: Benedict XVI
summary: Theologian, prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, and pope from 2005 to 2013. Author of Introduction to Christianity and the Jesus of Nazareth trilogy.

name: Henri de Lubac
summary: A leader of the return to the Church Fathers that shaped the Second Vatican Council, where he served as an expert adviser. Wrote Catholicism, Surnaturel, and The Splendor of the Church. Made a cardinal in 1983.

name: Hans Urs von Balthasar
summary: Read the whole faith through beauty, goodness, and truth in his trilogy The Glory of the Lord, Theo-Drama, and Theo-Logic. Co-founded the journal Communio with Ratzinger and de Lubac. Named a cardinal, he died two days before he was to receive the red hat.

name: John Paul II
title: Karol Wojtyła
summary: Philosopher and pope from 1978 to 2005. His Theology of the Body, encyclicals such as Veritatis Splendor and Fides et Ratio, and the Catechism of the Catholic Church he promulgated in 1992 shaped the Church's teaching for a generation. Canonized in 2014.
